name: CA-23
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+9 district with incumbent Jay Obernolte running for re-election
Overwhelming fundraising gap: $1.85M vs $127K raised, $1.38M vs $12K cash on hand
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about 3-4%
No public polls or expert ratings; national environment leans Democratic
model.rationale: The R+9 district, Obernolte's dominant financial position, and markets pricing a Democratic win near 3% all point to a comfortable Republican hold, with only the Democratic-leaning national environment offering Hodge any opening.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a closer race, or significant outside spending on Hodge's behalf, would be the clearest sign this is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 23rd District leans Republican by about nine points, and incumbent Jay Obernolte is seeking another term. He has raised roughly $1.9 million and holds $1.4 million in cash, while Democratic challenger Tessa Lynn Hodge has raised about $127,000 with just over $12,000 on hand. Outside spending has also favored Obernolte by a wide margin. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Hodge only about a 3% chance of winning. The main counterweight is the national political environment, which currently leans Democratic and could narrow margins in Republican-held districts. Even so, the combination of a favorable district, a well-funded incumbent, and a lightly funded challenger makes Obernolte a clear favorite, and the race is rated Likely Republican.
